$comment: The horde ladder. Ordered cheapest -> most capable. The NUMBER of rungs is the number of entries here: 3 models -> 3 rungs, 2 -> 2. The /delegate skill reads this to know which model serves which entropy band. Edit `model` to pin a rung to a specific model (alias haiku|sonnet|opus, or a full model id like claude-haiku-4-5-20251001). Optional `match` lists EVERY model id that serves the rung's band, so one rung can cover several models -- the top rung uses it because the orchestrator may be driven as opus or as fable, and a model on no rung is counted `untiered` and escapes the accounting fail-open. Add or remove a rung to change the ladder; the framework routes across whatever rungs exist. The HIGHEST rung (orchestrator: true) is the main agent / WARBOSS itself — work that lands there is decomposed or escalated, never dispatched to a subagent. Every lower rung is dispatched to the `doer` subagent with `model` set to that rung's model.

prices.$comment: BLENDED $/MILLION-tokens, used ONLY by the manual `scripts/ledger.mjs add` fallback (which has just an aggregate token count). The automatic hook path uses `pricing` below instead — prefer it. Set a model to null to log tokens only.

pricing.$comment: Per-class $/MILLION-tokens from the Anthropic price sheet fetched 2026-10-21 (see .warboss-horde/out/research-official.md). Used by both automatic meters via scripts/pricing.mjs, which prices EACH message: keys match a model id case-insensitively, longest key wins, and a key must end at a version boundary (end of id, '[', '@', or '-YYYYMMDD'), so an unlisted version prices as null instead of borrowing a neighbour's rate. cache_write is the 5-minute write, cache_write_1h the 1-hour write. `above` swaps in its rates when one request's prompt (input + cache read + cache write) exceeds prompt_tokens. Add every new model id here before driving it.

ladder.band: near-zero residual entropy — a literal machine could satisfy the contract: exact entry point, criteria as concrete input->expected, every second reading already killed
moderate residual entropy — decided but a literal machine would likely misread it: subtle invariants, non-trivial logic, or a slice that may need finer decomposition
high residual entropy — not yet decided. Stays with the WARBOSS (main agent): decompose, resolve forks, or escalate to the user. Never dispatched.
